SPTE 101.description: Examination of the functions and resources the university provides for students transitioning to college and the problems common to the first-year student-athlete experience.
SPTE 101.subject: SPTE
SPTE 101.title: The Student-Athlete Experience

SPTE 110.description: The American sport and entertainment enterprise: background, influences, and trends; collegiate and professional sport organizations; ownership and unionization; media portrayals.
SPTE 110.subject: SPTE
SPTE 110.title: Sport and Entertainment in American Life

SPTE 195.description: Introduction of networking, interviewing, and career planning in the sport and entertainment industry.
SPTE 195.subject: SPTE
SPTE 195.title: Sport and Entertainment Careers

SPTE 201.description: Introduction to sport management industry career fields.

SPTE 201.title: Introduction to Sport Management

SPTE 202.description: The study of underlying themes in entertainment management and its application to music, family shows, and other live entertainment business venues.
SPTE 202.subject: SPTE
SPTE 202.title: Introduction to Live Entertainment Management

SPTE 203.description: An overview of the history, impact, types, and trends of events and venues, the principles of event planning, the role of venues, and career options in each field.

SPTE 203.title: Introduction to Event and Venue Management

SPTE 240.description: Formation of contracts and their operation as they apply to business; promissory notes and checks; agency and employment.
SPTE 240.subject: SPTE
SPTE 240.title: Business Law

SPTE 274.description: Administrative tasks for computer usage, including software and hardware selection, applications, and solutions.
SPTE 274.subject: SPTE
SPTE 274.title: Computer Applications in Hospitality, Retail, and Sport Management

SPTE 295.description: Supervised work experience in a sport or entertainment management area selected by the student with approval of advisor. Contract approved by advisor or department chair is required for undergraduate students.
SPTE 295.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: SPTE 195, SPTE 201, SPTE 202, SPTE 203, SPTE 274 and MKTG 350.
SPTE 295.subject: SPTE
SPTE 295.title: Internship I in Sport and Entertainment Management

SPTE 302.description: This course focuses on the role of the manager in the entertainment industry and his or her relationships with artists, agents, buyers and industry executives.
SPTE 302.subject: SPTE
SPTE 302.title: Artist Representation and Management

SPTE 303.description: This course puts a fine point on performance tour management logistics, including booking, scheduling, shipping, budgeting, movement of equipment, and artist management challenges, including entertainment production.
SPTE 303.subject: SPTE
SPTE 303.title: Live Entertainment Tour Management

SPTE 305.description: The course is designed to present an overall view of the NASCAR industry through a series of guest speakers, who are subject matter experts in their respective NASCAR-related fields.
SPTE 305.subject: SPTE
SPTE 305.title: The Business of NASCAR

SPTE 310.description: Students are provided with an overview of college athletics. Though the course will cover the NJCAA and NAIA, it will particularly focus upon the NCAA, and more specifically, upon the business of “Big-Time” intercollegiate athletics.
SPTE 310.subject: SPTE
SPTE 310.title: Collegiate Athletics

SPTE 315.description: Students will gain a basic understanding of NCAA Division I rules and regulations while learning how the rules are applied to member institution. An overview of the operations of an NCAA Division I compliance office and coaching regulations will be provided as well.
SPTE 315.subject: SPTE
SPTE 315.title: NCAA Compliance

SPTE 320.description: Laws and regulatory bodies affecting the management of sport personnel, facilities, and events.
SPTE 320.subject: SPTE
SPTE 320.title: Sport and the Law

SPTE 325.description: Management of club and resort sport complexes.
SPTE 325.subject: SPTE
SPTE 325.title: Resort and Club Recreation Programming

SPTE 330.description: Examination of the Summer Olympic Games and its impact on sport, entertainment, hospitality, tourism and the host community.
SPTE 330.subject: SPTE
SPTE 330.title: The Summer Olympic Games

SPTE 335.description: Overall view of the sport of baseball from a business perspective.
SPTE 335.subject: SPTE
SPTE 335.title: The Business of Baseball

SPTE 340.description: Principles of manufacturing and retailing applied to the sporting goods industry.
SPTE 340.subject: SPTE
SPTE 340.title: The Sporting Goods Industry

SPTE 342.description: The formation and negotiation of contracts in Sport and Entertainment Management.
SPTE 342.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: SPTE 240 or ACCT 324 or equivalent.
SPTE 342.subject: SPTE
SPTE 342.title: Sport and Entertainment Contracts and Negotiations

SPTE 350.description: Exploration of the transformative impact of generative artificial intelligence (AI) on the sport and entertainment industries.
SPTE 350.subject: SPTE
SPTE 350.title: Generative AI in Sport and Entertainment Management

SPTE 376.description: Theoretical and practical approaches to managing risk in Sport and Entertainment venues and events.
SPTE 376.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: SPTE 240 or ACCT 324 or equivalent.
SPTE 376.subject: SPTE
SPTE 376.title: Risk Management in Sport and Entertainment

SPTE 380.description: Marketing theory and practice and how it relates and applies to sport and entertainment.
SPTE 380.subject: SPTE
SPTE 380.title: Sport and Entertainment Marketing

SPTE 385.description: The objective of this course is to familiarize students with the ethical issues that exist in the business of sport and entertainment. Students will learn theories of ethics and how they relate to issues faced by managers in the sport and entertainment industry. Ethical theories and philosophies – deontology, utilitarianism, and virtue - will be driving the discussions and understandings of ethical decision-making in this class.
SPTE 385.subject: SPTE
SPTE 385.title: Ethics in Sport and Entertainment Business

SPTE 399.description: Students will have an opportunity to explore a specific area of sport and entertainment management. Individual students will indentify an area of study related to sport and entertainment management and complete a research paper on this topic under the guidance of the instructor.
SPTE 399.subject: SPTE
SPTE 399.title: Independent Study

SPTE 402.description: Performing arts and entertainment industries’ social, economic, and legal issues, in addition to the development and role of entertainment in society, will be analyzed–from its roots to the present.
SPTE 402.subject: SPTE
SPTE 402.title: Entertainment and the Law

SPTE 404.description: This course should provide students with an understanding of various methods of promotion and approaches to the application of advertising and publicity in the broad spectrum of modern media.
SPTE 404.subject: SPTE
SPTE 404.title: Promoting Entertainment Events

SPTE 410.description: Investigation of sport and entertainment as critical facets of American society.
SPTE 410.subject: SPTE
SPTE 410.title: Sport and Entertainment in Popular Culture

SPTE 430.description: Basic principles required to promote a service marketing strategy in sport and entertainment.
SPTE 430.subject: SPTE
SPTE 430.title: Sport and Entertainment Services Marketing

SPTE 435.description: Programming, marketing, public relations, fiscal considerations, operation, labor relations, personnel, and event management for spectator sports and entertainment events.
SPTE 435.subject: SPTE
SPTE 435.title: Spectator Facilities Management

SPTE 440.description: Economic and finance theories applied to the management of sport and entertainment organizations.
SPTE 440.subject: SPTE
SPTE 440.title: Sport and Entertainment Business and Finance

SPTE 444.description: Application of management principles to sports and entertainment events.
SPTE 444.subject: SPTE
SPTE 444.title: Sports and Entertainment Event Management

SPTE 450.description: Students will be provided with an overview of the sales process and learn how the sales process applies to sport and entertainment while using hands on exercises to perpetuate the understanding of the importance of sales.
SPTE 450.subject: SPTE
SPTE 450.title: Sales in Sport and Entertainment Business

SPTE 477.description: Introduction to the specialized field of commercial real estate development for hospitality, tourism, retail, sport, and entertainment industries, covering the entire development process from site selection and market analysis to financing, design, construction, and asset management.
SPTE 477.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in FINA 366.
SPTE 477.subject: SPTE
SPTE 477.title: Commercial Real Estate Development for the HRSM Industries

SPTE 490.description: Current topics and trends in sport, live entertainment, and venue management. Content varies by title. May be repeated once.
SPTE 490.subject: SPTE
SPTE 490.title: Special Topics in Sport and Entertainment Management

SPTE 495.description: Placement with a sport or entertainment organization for a supervised learning experience in the student’s career specialization area.
SPTE 495.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in SPTE 440 and SPTE 444; 114 credit hours.
SPTE 495.subject: SPTE
SPTE 495.title: Internship II in Sport and Entertainment Management

SPTE 498.description: Working with a faculty mentor, students develop a research project and related research skills.
SPTE 498.subject: SPTE
SPTE 498.title: Research Experience

SPTE 499.description: A senior thesis related to one of the advanced courses in the major program.
SPTE 499.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: minimum GPA of 3.50 in major courses, 3.30 overall.
SPTE 499.subject: SPTE
SPTE 499.title: Senior Thesis

SPTE 501.description: Trends and Issues in Sport and Entertainment Management.
SPTE 501.subject: SPTE
SPTE 501.title: Trends and Issues in Sport and Entertainment Management

SPTE 515.description: Classic and contemporary, international and domestic sports films featuring heroes and villains from baseball, basketball, boxing, football, soccer and other sports stages. Rhetorical analysis of socially significant sport films after exposure to numerous critical perspectives.
SPTE 515.subject: SPTE
SPTE 515.title: Sport in Film

SPTE 545.description: Recruiting, hiring, training, and retaining part-time employees and volunteers in sport and entertainment.
SPTE 545.subject: SPTE
SPTE 545.title: Managing Part-Time Employees and Volunteers

SPTE 550.description: This course is designed to provide students with an overview of the business of esports. It will focus on the history of video games from creation to the present and will also cover the various business elements of the modern, competitive esports environment.
SPTE 550.subject: SPTE
SPTE 550.title: The Business of Esports

SPTE 560.description: The study of performing arts management as it relates to nonprofits and organizational structure.
SPTE 560.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in SPTE 202 and SPTE 380.
SPTE 560.subject: SPTE
SPTE 560.title: Performing Arts Management and Leadership

SPTE 565.description: The study of the management of Broadway productions from script to play, including the creative process, business ventures, production houses, and investor relations.
SPTE 565.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: SPTE 202 and SPTE 380; C or higher for SPTE majors.
SPTE 565.subject: SPTE
SPTE 565.title: Business of Broadway

SPTE 570.description: This course examines a variety of global sport and entertainment management issues. The emphasis will be on an understanding of the concepts related to the sport and entertainment management in an international setting. Content varies by title. May be repeated once.
SPTE 570.subject: SPTE
SPTE 570.title: Special Topics in Global Sport

SPTE 580.description: Business principles in the management of public and private sector sport programs.
SPTE 580.subject: SPTE
SPTE 580.title: Business Principles in Sport Management.

SPTE 585.description: This course focuses on issues relevant to sport, entertainment, and related industries. The goal of the class will be for students to understand both basic and complex concepts within economics in a sport and entertainment context, in order to grasp the importance of economic decision-making.
SPTE 585.subject: SPTE
SPTE 585.title: Sports Economics

SPTE 590.description: Investigation of Special topics pertinent to the sport and entertainment management industry. Content varies by title. May be repeated twice.
SPTE 590.subject: SPTE
SPTE 590.title: Special Topics in Live Entertainment and Sport

SPTE 635.description: Business concepts needed to develop sport and entertainment special events.
SPTE 635.subject: SPTE
SPTE 635.title: Sport and Entertainment Event Development

SPTE 640.description: Managing public assembly facilities and venues.
SPTE 640.subject: SPTE
SPTE 640.title: Venue Management: Principles and Practices

SPTE 650.description: Use of integrated marketing communication concepts, theories, and strategies in sport and entertainment.
SPTE 650.subject: SPTE
SPTE 650.title: Integrated Marketing Communication in Sport and Entertainment

SPTE 655.description: In-depth investigation of social networks, digital platforms, and online marketing for the live entertainment and sport industries.
SPTE 655.subject: SPTE
SPTE 655.title: Social Media in Live Entertainment and Sport

SPTE 701.description: Management principles in the sport and entertainment industry.
SPTE 701.subject: SPTE
SPTE 701.title: Management in the Sport and Entertainment Industry

SPTE 720.description: The advanced study of underlying themes in entertainment management and its application to music, family shows, and other live entertainment business venues.
SPTE 720.subject: SPTE
SPTE 720.title: Advanced Live Entertainment Management

SPTE 730.description: Advanced knowledge of the legal issues that frequently arise in the context of sport will be covered. The focus of the course is law as it applies to sport as well as how the law affects participants, spectators, sport organizations, and facility managers, among others.
SPTE 730.subject: SPTE
SPTE 730.title: Advanced Sport and the Law

SPTE 736.description: Process of new venture creation with respect to sport and entertainment events.
SPTE 736.subject: SPTE
SPTE 736.title: Sport and Entertainment Event Entrepreneurship

SPTE 746.description: The risks and security issues associated with managing public assembly facilities.
SPTE 746.subject: SPTE
SPTE 746.title: Risk and Security Management in Public Assembly Facilities

SPTE 750.description: Policy development and implementation in the sport and entertainment industry.
SPTE 750.subject: SPTE
SPTE 750.title: Strategic Planning and Policy Development in Sport and Entertainment Management

SPTE 760.description: This course is designed to provide a foundation in the principles of sport and entertainment marketing.
SPTE 760.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: Undergraduate marketing class or equivalent.
SPTE 760.subject: SPTE
SPTE 760.title: Principles of Sport and Entertainment Marketing

SPTE 765.description: Comparative approaches of revenue generation and sales processes/strategies used by sport and entertainment organizations.
SPTE 765.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: Completion of an introductory marketing course and/or relevant industry marketing experience.
SPTE 765.subject: SPTE
SPTE 765.title: Advanced Sales in Sport and Entertainment Management

SPTE 780.title: Public Assembly Facility Operations and Procedures

SPTE 781.description: Examination of the Olympic Games, a mega sport and tourism event, and its impact on the sport, entertainment, hospitality and tourism sectors.
SPTE 781.subject: SPTE
SPTE 781.title: Seminar on the Olympic Games

SPTE 790.description: This course examines financial information necessary to perform the usual duties and responsibilities associated with sport facilities, programs and organizations.
SPTE 790.subject: SPTE
SPTE 790.title: Sport and Entertainment Finance

SPTE 798.description: Independent study for advanced students under faculty supervision. May be taken twice for degree credit.
SPTE 798.subject: SPTE
SPTE 798.title: Directed Study in Sport and Entertainment Management

SPTE 799.description: Thesis preparation in sport and entertainment management.
SPTE 799.subject: SPTE
SPTE 799.title: Thesis Preparation

SPTE 801.description: Acquaints sport management PhD students with advanced principles and applications of the sport and entertainment management discipline. This course will expose the doctoral student to research examining organization, leadership, and strategic management in the sport and entertainment industry and appropriate sub-industries.
SPTE 801.subject: SPTE
SPTE 801.title: Seminar in SPTE Management

SPTE 810.description: Provides Sport and Entertainment Management graduate students with insights that foster professional growth and development as a college instructor. This course examines the scholarship of teaching SPTE and developing optimal classroom environments and identification and guided reflective analysis of critical issues in SPTE education.
SPTE 810.subject: SPTE
SPTE 810.title: Seminar in SPTE Education

SPTE 830.description: Acquaints students with advanced theory and application of law and risk management in sport and entertainment management through the review of scholarship about professional and amateur sport, laws impacting the entertainment industry, and risk management issues within sport and entertainment facilities.
SPTE 830.subject: SPTE
SPTE 830.title: Seminar SPTE Law Risk Management

SPTE 860.description: Acquaints sport management PhD students with advanced principles and application of the sport and entertainment marketing discipline. The course will take an in-depth look at how amateur/professional sport, and emerging sport business enterprises and trends affect the practice of sport and entertainment marketing. This course is designed for students to study sport and entertainment marketing theories and practical applications and principles by specifically learning about marketing information systems, pricing strategies, media relations, promotional methods and endorsements.
SPTE 860.subject: SPTE
SPTE 860.title: Seminar in SPTE Marketing

SPTE 880.description: When sport is discussed, how we talk about them, and the possible viewpoints are all given beforehand by deeply entrenched social institutions. The objective of this course is to identify how these institutions are constructed, and how sport is an activity that embodies social relations.
SPTE 880.subject: SPTE
SPTE 880.title: Sport and Society

SPTE 889.description: Through presentation of scholarly readings and immersion into one’s own in-depth research project, this course explores a variety of qualitative research approaches, taking into account issues of epistemology, methodology, and representation. It is designed to help students develop an understanding of qualitative research methods and designs.
SPTE 889.subject: SPTE
SPTE 889.title: Qualitative Inquiry in Sport and Entertainment Management

SPTE 890.description: This course covers advanced principles and applications of sport and entertainment finance. The course takes an in-depth look at the theory, concepts, and frameworks of sport and entertainment finance research. The focus will be on the optimum financial policies and decisions of nonfinancial firms in the sport and entertainment industry.
SPTE 890.subject: SPTE
SPTE 890.title: Seminar in SPTE Finance

SPTE 899.description: Assists students through the proposal and dissertation writing process.
SPTE 899.subject: SPTE
SPTE 899.title: Dissertation Preparation
